clue.text: 20's schmuck eating metal, different inhaling nitrogen, it follows

indicators.note: the fool's word takes the following string into its mouth, so it encloses them

parts.note: schmuck and putz are both Yiddish-derived American slang for a fool

indicators.note: the little word it comes after the pieces before it, placed at the end of the inner run

parts.note: tin is a metallic element

indicators.note: the word for different breathes in the gas symbol, holding it inside

parts.note: different means other
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
taken as written

explanation.surface: An insult is hurled at someone who swallowed metal and breathed in a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is BERLIN, here the songwriter Irving Berlin; 'schmuck' is Yiddish-American slang for a fool. 'inhaling' puts N inside the word for different, and 'eating' wraps the fool round the whole inner run.
explanation.definitionFit: Puttin' on the Ritz is a famous song written by Irving Berlin, number 20 of the theme.

clue.text: Become stiff absorbing one's heat

indicators.note: the phrase for dying soaks up the numeral, holding it inside

parts.note: to become a stiff, slang for a corpse, is to die or pass on
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something hardens as it takes in warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become stiff' looks physical, but a stiff is a corpse, so it means die: PASS ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat in the sense of intense feeling or ardour is a synonym of strong emotion, passion.

clue.text: See 4
Tooth in canine a figure's lost is gold

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters of a figure are said to be lost from the word canine, leaving only its first letter

parts.note: a figure here is the number nine, so A plus NINE
taken as written
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A dentist's riddle: a dog's fang that loses a number turns into gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking A NINE out of CANINE leaves just C. OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is one of the front cutting teeth, an example of a tooth.

clue.text: 20's adaptations, with title he made up

indicators.note: the letters are made up into a new arrangement, invented afresh

explanation.surface: A writer describes how he concocted versions of a work and gave them a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is BERLIN, the songwriter Irving Berlin. All 22 letters of 'adaptations with title he' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Hat, White Tie and Tails is a well-known Irving Berlin song from the film Top Hat.

clue.text: Islands or island around the north

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the island word goes around the compass letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a key is a low island or reef, as in the Florida Keys
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A geography question asks about some islands, or perhaps one island, up in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: ORKNEY is a group of islands off the far north of Scotland, which fits the surface's 'north' too.
explanation.definitionFit: Orkney is an archipelago off northern Scotland, so the name denotes a group of islands.

clue.text: Number of thugs, German, holding soldier John up

indicators.note: the German name holds the reversed pair inside it

parts.note: Hans is a typical German man's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pair of words is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
john is slang for a toilet, as is loo

explanation.surface: A gang of thugs, a German among them, lifts a soldier called John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a numeral here: a number of thugs is a group. GILOO turned up gives OOLIG inside HANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooligans are violent rowdy youths, so the plural word names a group of thugs.

clue.text: Most insignificant little bird circling European river, endlessly rising

indicators.note: the bird's name goes round the reversed river, enclosing it

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the trimmed river name is read upwards, backwards
endlessly says the river's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the Seine flows through Paris

explanation.surface: A tiny bird flies in circles above a French river as it climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the river's last E, giving SEIN; 'rising' turns that upwards to NIES in this down clue, and 'circling' sets it inside the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiniest is the superlative of tiny, so it means the smallest or least significant.

clue.text: Important agreements keeping church in fuel are new relationships

indicators.note: the fuel word keeps the church letters inside it

parts.note: peat is burnt as fuel
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: new says the following short word is given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: ties are bonds or relationships

explanation.surface: Big deals that put the church into the fuel business create new partnerships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ARE into REA.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace treaties are formal settlements between nations, about as important as agreements get.

clue.text: Drink requiring 15 25 stomach?

indicators.note: the stomach is the inner part of the body, so the drink is found in the inside of the cross-referenced phrase

parts.note: 15 and 25 together give the phrase meaning certain, a word for metal that is unbreakable

explanation.surface: A drink so harsh you need a cast-iron stomach to take it.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 25 is CAST-IRON; its inside, without the first C and the final RON, gives the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so it is a drink.

clue.text: 20's reason fool follows regular pattern

indicators.note: the pair reason and fool follows the pattern word, so they come after it

parts.note: a check is a pattern of regular squares
a point is a reason or argument
a charlie is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Someone explains why an idiot copies a set design.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is BERLIN, here the city. CHARLIE as a fool is British slang ('a right charlie').
explanation.definitionFit: Checkpoint Charlie was the best-known crossing point in the Berlin Wall during the Cold War.

clue.text: Wife, seeing girl with husband, blowing top and ditching ring

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman

indicators.note: blowing top says the first letter of what remains is lost
ditching says a word for a ring is thrown out of the word husband

parts.note: a band is a ring, as on a finger

explanation.surface: A wife sees a girl with her husband, loses her temper and throws away her wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's angry wife misleads: 'blowing top' and 'ditching ring' both act on the printed word husband, removing its first letter and a word for a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is an informal word for a man's wife.

clue.text: Short man of the cloth cut a few sharp lines?

indicators.note: short says the word for a clergyman is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a cleric is a clergyman, a man of the cloth
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: A clergyman of small stature trims some pointed verses.
explanation.walkthrough: A clerihew is a comic four-line verse about a famous person, invented by E. C. Bentley.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a short witty biographical poem, so a few sharp lines describes it well.

clue.text: See 1
Person after death's represented — here?

parts.note: one means a person, as in 'one should'

explanation.surface: Where a person is commemorated after death.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DEATHS plus ONE are rearranged; the whole clue then describes where the answer stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone stands at a grave, the place where a dead person is marked and commemorated.

clue.text: Certain to find a prison in prisoner

indicators.note: in places the article and slang word inside the prisoner word

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to find a jail cell inside a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-iron as an adjective means unbreakable, so a cast-iron guarantee is certain.

clue.text: Drop down to pinch women's booty

indicators.note: the drooping word pinches the letter, gripping it inside

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop down
W is an abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A thief crouches down to steal some women's loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinch' looks like stealing, fitting the surface, but it signals holding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is slang for stolen goods or plunder, the same as booty.

clue.text: Very proper request

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
licit means lawful or proper

explanation.surface: A thoroughly correct appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask for or seek, so it is a verb meaning request.

clue.text: 20's right, case to be reassessed

indicators.note: reassessed says the letters are looked at again and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A lawyer says Berlin is in the right and the case must be heard again.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is BERLIN, here the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reichstag is the parliament building in Berlin, home to the German Bundestag.

clue.text: See 10
A son of the Empire State bearing daughter, no one specific

explanation.definitionFit: Anybody means any person at all, so it refers to no one specific.

clue.text: European city sees African country losing heart to characters in opposition?

indicators.note: the central letter of the country's name is lost, given up in favour of the following characters

explanation.walkthrough: The heart of BENIN is its middle N; swap it for R and L, the letters for right and left.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin is the capital city of Germany, a European city.

clue.text: Sell pint that's dodgy, getting wasted

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound or shifty, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A barman sells a dubious pint and the customer gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' looks like drunk, fitting the surface, but means squandered.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-spent means squandered or used badly, the sense of wasted as in wasted money.

clue.text: 20's sailing boat capsizing in middle of Wash

indicators.note: in places the overturned boat inside the middle letters
the middle of the word Wash is its central pair of letters
a capsized boat turns over, so the boat's name is written backwards

parts.note: a yawl is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A sailing boat overturns in the middle of the Wash, a bay on England's east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is BERLIN, here Irving Berlin. The Wash is a bay on the east coast of England. 'capsizing' turns the boat's name over, and 'in' places it inside the middle of Wash.
explanation.definitionFit: Always is a 1925 song written by Irving Berlin.

clue.text: See 4
First of students taking alcohol, sozzled, scoffing me for his dinner?
